## What is an Agent

- An agent is an AI helper that can edit code for you
- You describe a task, and it works directly in your files
- It can create files, edit files, and run commands
- You review the changes and keep the ones you want

## What is an Agent Harness

- A harness is the program that connects an LLM to your files
- It gives the LLM access to a project's files, a terminal, and Git
- Without a harness, an LLM can only talk - it cannot touch your files
- A codespace can run more than one harness

## Some Agent Harnesses

- **OpenCode** - an open source harness that works with many models
- **Claude Code** - Anthropic's harness
- **Codex** - OpenAI's harness
- All of them read a prompt, edit files, and can run commands
- They differ mainly in which company built them and which models they use most easily

## Create a Repository from a Template

1. Open [github.com/calvinw/ai-agentic-tools-template](https://github.com/calvinw/ai-agentic-tools-template)
2. Click **Use this template**
3. Select **Create a new repository**
4. Name your repository
5. Click **Create repository from template**

## What the Template Provides

- The repository holds only configuration files
- The codespace image already has OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex installed
- No installing anything yourself
- Every harness is ready to run as soon as the codespace starts

## Open the Repository in a Codespace

1. Open your new repository's **Code** page
2. Click the green **Code** button
3. Select the **Codespaces** tab
4. Click **Create codespace on main**
5. Wait for the dev container to finish building

## Start OpenCode

1. Open a terminal in the codespace
2. Run `opencode.sh`
3. OpenCode starts and is ready for a prompt

`opencode.sh` starts OpenCode with permissions already set to allow reading, writing, and running commands.

## Select a Free Model

- OpenCode can use models from many different providers
- Some models cost nothing to use
- Type `/models` inside OpenCode to see the list
- Choose a free model, such as **MiniMax M2.5 Free**

## Give OpenCode a Task

- Type a prompt describing what you want, such as fixing a bug or adding a feature
- OpenCode reads your files, plans the change, and edits them
- It can run commands, such as tests, to check its own work
- It shows you what it changed as it works

## Review and Commit the Changes

1. Read what OpenCode changed before trusting it
2. Open the **Source Control** view to see the changed files
3. Stage the changes you want to keep
4. Commit and push, the same as any other codespace change
